title: Living Creatures: Exploring their Characteristics
seo_title: Living Creatures Class 6 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Curiosity Chapter 10)
standard_text: Characteristics of living things: growth, nutrition, respiration, excretion, response to stimuli, movement and reproduction; conditions for seed germination; life cycles of plants and animals such as the frog and the mosquito (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 10).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 6 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 10: living and non-living things, growth, respiration, excretion, response to stimuli, reproduction, seed germination and life cycles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Living things grow, breathe, respond and reproduce.
key_sub: Seeds need water, air and warmth to germinate.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living things share characteristics: they need food, respire, excrete wastes, respond to stimuli such as touch and light, grow, move and reproduce. A car moves and uses fuel, but it cannot grow or reproduce, so it is not living. A seed is alive but resting.

Seeds germinate only with water, air and a suitable temperature. Living things go through a life cycle: a frog goes from egg to tadpole to froglet to adult; a mosquito from egg to larva to pupa to adult.

Example

Seeds under boiled, cooled water do not germinate. Why?

boiling removes air

Answer: seeds need air

Example

Mimosa leaves fold when touched. Which characteristic?

reaction to touch

Answer: response to stimuli

Common mistakes

  • Calling something living just because it moves.
  • Thinking seeds need sunlight to germinate.
  • Thinking plants do not respire.

items.q: What is nutrition, as a characteristic of living things?
c: producing young ones of the same kind
reacting to changes around, such as touch, light or heat

items.e: Nutrition: taking in food to get energy and materials.

items.e: Reproduction: producing young ones of the same kind.
